content:
The Program/Circuit model is basically a universal algebraic sort of circuit. However, there is one quirk that diverges from this: constants. In particular, we represent constants as gates. This has the quirk that in lower bound proofs I am working on, often I end up counting the positive arity gates for the "true size". The way to think about why constants aren't gates is that gates are like constraints between different "variables", where you can think of both wires and inputs as "variables". Constants actually don't really introduce another constraint, so they don't have the same impact on complexity.

My proposed fix is to add to the Signature a Con type and interpretation will have to interpret constants as well. This will make the code a bit more complex, and I think we should also constrain the arity of functions to be >=1, so I wanted to discuss it here.

There is a further generalization here where we can actually make Signature into Vocabulary from Finite Model Theory, which basically just means adding relation symbols as well (which will be uninhabited for Circuits) and we could potentially talk about circuits and descriptive complexity in the same language, which would be really powerful potentially for connecting those fields.

Anyone have thoughts or feelings?
For context, we should definitely add finite model theory at some point, as first order reductions/projections are a really natural thing in complexity theory and there are lots of relevant theorems.
cc @Christian Reitwiessner @Aviv Bar Natan
I don’t fully understand but if we are staying in the „gates are constraints“ model, we could also extend wires to be either outputs of other gates or any constant.
But extending this to support finite model theory certainly sounds like a good goal :slight_smile:

I prefer the current version, I really like the flexibility here.
I think the solution should be changing the way we measure size to be customizable, like you added a count per type of gate.

we could also extend wires to be either outputs of other gates or any constant

This is basically my proposal by the way, Con will be used in Wire.

the solution should be changing the way we measure size to be customizable, like you added a count per type of gate

I think we should enable this ergonomically no matter what, for instance for the AND/XOR basis where we like to count ANDs and other various reasons. My argument against using the operation for these constants is that it is sort of "semantically wrong". I don't think we lose any flexibility by allowing Con, we just lose and add some precision for readers. Otherwise the size field on circuits is kind of a lie...

I quite like the parsimony of the current version so could be convinced to keep it, I love how pedagogically clear it is, but to me this is the one "nit" where it diverges from other more standard circuit representations like let-chains where they typically have values either being variables or constants.

Sam Schlesinger said:

I don't think we lose any flexibility by allowing Con, we just lose and add some precision for readers.

You mean because one could use Con := Empty? This is technically true, but seems to complicate things.
You're forcing the user to use constants in a certain way, and also if you're going to remove 0-arity gates that means users need a second inductive of 0-arity gates to pass to Con.
This sounds complicated for users, whereas providing fancier size functions sounds great.

You mean because one could use Con := Empty?

Yes, exactly.

You're forcing the user to use constants in a certain way, and also if you're going to remove 0-arity gates that means users need a second inductive of 0-arity gates to pass to Con.

It is more syntax for users, but it might actually make more sense than knowing that you can't just "use constants" and then realizing you have to add them to your ops. Either way we should clarify it with docs.

I also quite like the idea of merging it all together with finite model theory, then it enables us to have a single homomorphism definition and other niceties like that. We'll save a lot of code down the line...

Does something like this not solve the issue?

def Circuit.count (f : σ.Op → Bool) : Nat := ...

(count all gates that f returns true for)
Yes, we should have something like that but with Nat instead of Bool and other way.

You mean

def Circuit.count {α : Type*} [AddCommMonoid α] (cost : σ.Op → α) : α := ...

? This sounds good to me, although if we keep generalizing we'll reach Circuit.eval, but the point was to give a simple count function.

Not sure what you mean by "other way"

Sorry, was a bit busy earlier. The reason you want it to return AddCommMonoid is that you can do something interesting where you abstract out circuit operations and then use circuit translations from the higher-level operations to the lower-level ones, and often you'll want to have different costs for the different operations. An example would be if we compiled a function on finite field elements or vector space elements into a Boolean circuit.
Usually it would be Nat but I guess it could also be Real
Actually, conceivably some folks would use vectors too.
